extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying for MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships (HE-MSCA-2023-PF), particularly applicants to NTNU
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required evaluation criteria for preparing Part B (project description, work plan, host capacity, CV, ethics, environment, letters) of an MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship proposal (HE‑MSCA‑2023‑PF), with NTNU-specific tips. Targets applicants drafting proposals and host institutions completing Part B/Part B2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of Work Packages and allocation of resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the timing of your various Work Packages and their duration so evaluators can understand feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight feasibility of WPs, tasks, Deliverables and Milestones; explain timing and durations in section 3.1; show how overlapping WPs will be managed and any resources that facilitate tasks (existing techniques, prior experience, technician support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight facilitators and in‑kind contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Make explicit any resources, institutional experience or in‑kind contributions (e.g. NTNU support) that will facilitate completing tasks and staying within budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State if techniques are already established at the host, you have prior experience, or you will receive technician or institutional support. If an important in‑kind contribution exists, make it clear so evaluators can judge achievability vs available budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be realistic; avoid over‑ambitious planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Project timing and effort estimates should be realistic; underestimating effort undermines credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TIP: Being over‑ambitious (underestimating effort) casts doubt on ability to achieve objectives and will lose marks. Rework project if high likelihood×high impact risks exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label deliverables, milestones and risks coherently
rubrics_metrics.description: Label deliverables, milestones and risks (e.g. D1.1) and make them visible in the narrative to ensure coherence across sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TIP: Cross‑reference labels in methodology (section 1.2 or section 2.2 for communication/dissemination) to give evaluators a clear understanding of the work plan when reading section 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress monitoring, risks and mitigation (cover scientific and administrative risks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a convincing overview of risks (scientific and non‑scientific) and suitable contingency/mitigation plans for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover administrative, technological, developmental risks etc.; explaining risks and mitigations demonstrates project maturity. Use a table listing risks, likelihood, consequence and mitigation. If only a table is provided, present mitigation measures narratively elsewhere for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe project management arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the project will be managed day‑to‑day and how progress will be monitored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe who manages the project (usually you with supervisor support), frequency of meetings (weekly meetings, quarterly reviews), supervisory structure, and institutional support (EU research advisors, legal/financial/IP experts). Mention NTNU support services that will help during grant preparation and project lifetime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk table structure and content
rubrics_metrics.description: List critical risks per Work Package with likelihood, impact and mitigation strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a table with columns: Risk; Mitigation measures; Likelihood; Impact on the work; Alternative strategies. Explain why unlikely risks are unlikely in mitigation column. Prefer narrative descriptions for mitigation to aid clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid high‑likelihood, high‑impact risks
rubrics_metrics.description: A plan that contains risks that are both high consequence and high likelihood indicates need to redesign the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TIP: Do not have any high consequence, high likelihood risks; if present, redesign the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gantt chart completeness and alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a complete Gantt chart capturing all Work Packages, Deliverables, Milestones, training, communication, dissemination, exploitation activities and secondments/placements, aligned with the work plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators will scrutinize the Gantt chart; include a legend and explain what listed items correspond to (or describe them in the main text). Check timing carefully. Ask EU adviser for redacted successful examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hosting arrangements and integration in team
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how you will be integrated into the scientific and social working environment at the host to show you will not be left alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific (not generic). Explain support services, integration measures (social events, seminars, teaching you might contribute to), and how integration contributes to two‑way knowledge/skill transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two‑way transfer of knowledge and skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate how integration will enable transfer of knowledge/skills from you to the research group and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear benefits to both researcher and host; provide concrete examples of knowledge exchange and planned activities that enable transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisor profile and supervision plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the supervisor's track record, expertise, and supervision arrangements (frequency, formats) to demonstrate quality of supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight supervisor's qualifications and experience supervising early career researchers, proposed meeting frequency (weekly one‑on‑one, lab meetings), and commitment to appraisals/personal development reviews as per MSCA Guidelines for Supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research group description and integration measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the research group's interests, size, trainees, complementarity with you and concrete measures for your integration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention publications and achievements, collaboration mechanisms, social integration measures (local seminars, workshops), possible teaching contributions, and how you will collaborate with the group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended collaborations and interdisciplinarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain intended collaborations with the host and measures ensuring interdisciplinary or multi‑disciplinary aspects benefit the Fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify how expertise and methods from different disciplines will be brought together, how the host will facilitate interdisciplinary exposure beyond the supervisor's group, and justify if interdisciplinarity is not relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: International networking and conference attendance opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe opportunities for establishing new international contacts and attending conferences during the Fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how both you and the host group will benefit from new contacts and how conference attendance is planned to support objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support services available from host (administrative and researcher support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail institutional support available (EU advisors, legal/financial/IP experts, International Researcher Support Office) and how they will help with administrative, legal, financial, relocation and social integration issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: immigration, tax, housing, childcare advice; social events; language cafés and free Norwegian language courses; administrative project support for EU projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and capacity of participating organisations (infrastructure, logistics, facilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Convince evaluators you will have access to all required infrastructures, logistics and facilities to carry out the project successfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate facilities explicitly to your objectives/WPs; describe state‑of‑the‑art equipment, trained staff, relevant software licences; provide more detail in Part B2 Section 5 (Capacity of Participating Organisations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementarity of secondment / non‑academic placement
rubrics_metrics.description: If secondments or non‑academic placements are included, demonstrate what complementary infrastructure/logistics the partner provides and how this benefits the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how the secondment institution's facilities differ from the host's and demonstrate complementarity between institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part B2 CV length and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: CV of the researcher should be approximately 5 pages and fully consistent with information in Part A and B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dd/mm/yyyy date format, present subsections in reverse chronological order (most recent first), and clearly explain career gaps or unconventional paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: CV: required basic elements
rubrics_metrics.description: At minimum, the CV must include the researcher's name, professional experience (most recent first with exact dates), and education including PhD award date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide exact dates in dd/mm/yyyy format; include doctoral award date or viva date as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and research outputs reporting (open access and qualitative assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: List publications and other outputs (data, software, algorithms) expected to be open access where possible, accompanied by a very short qualitative assessment of their scientific significance (do not use Journal Impact Factor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate peer‑reviewed journals, conference proceedings, monographs, and other outputs; provide concise statements on significance and avoid mentioning JIF (explicit note: do NOT mention the Journal Impact Factor). Upload preprints where appropriate and include DOIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other CV items to include
rubrics_metrics.description: Include invited presentations, conference organisation, led research expeditions, granted patents, industrial innovation participation, prizes/awards, funding received, supervising and mentoring activities, and other relevant items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific and give context (e.g. event names, roles). These items strengthen the CV and illustrate breadth of experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD defence and eligibility timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis before the call deadline but have not yet been formally awarded the degree must indicate the viva date; defence after the deadline makes the applicant ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state the date of the successful PhD defence. Researchers defending after the call deadline will be automatically declared ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use CV pages to demonstrate career‑stage‑appropriate strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the allotted CV pages to demonstrate a strong CV relative to career stage, showcasing skills, competences, achievements and commitment to good science (e.g. open science).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TIP: Showcase alignment between research experience and proposed project; include open science practices, mentoring, funding track record and other relevant achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare and explain career gaps or unconventional paths
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state any career gaps (parental leave, illness, military service) or unconventional career paths so evaluators can assess CV fairly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear explanation statements to allow fair assessment and context for career progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a personal statement / research profile summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a brief personal statement (half to two‑thirds of a page) summarising who you are, what drives you, past achievements and vision and how the Fellowship supports your aspirations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bold for key points. Possible titles: Research profile and major achievements; Research track record and main achievements to date. Explain how the Fellowship is a perfect fit (you, project, training, supervisor, host).

rubrics_metrics.name: How to present publication record
rubrics_metrics.description: When presenting publications, include a short summary statement, use sub‑headings (peer‑reviewed, under review, non‑English), provide full references, and clarify authorship contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight your last name in bold in author lists; indicate co‑first or corresponding author; highlight publications without your PhD supervisor; include a short statement of your contribution and the publication's contribution/impact; separate peer‑reviewed and under review; for under review prefer preprints with DOI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference and invited talk reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: When listing invited presentations, specify event name (not just acronym), location, whether invited or selected, title of talk/poster and specify the format (talk/poster).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify selection mechanism (invited vs selected/via competition) and note any postponements/cancellations due to COVID‑19.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prizes and awards reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: When describing prizes and awards, include the funder's full name, state the award value in Euros, and indicate profile/importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report all awards, even small ones (travel grants, best poster), and make clear when an award is high‑profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervision and mentoring experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any supervising/mentoring activities broadly (undergrad, master's, PhD students, peers, expeditions, training), indicating scope and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the types of trainees, projects supervised, and any coordination or mentoring roles you held; be explicit about the methodologies or training provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe major collaborations with concrete outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: List major collaborations, clarify linking topics, and signpost concrete activities or outputs (papers in preparation, visits) to demonstrate established network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about the topic linking you to collaborators and any tangible outputs (one paper in preparation, upcoming research stay, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overview of participating organisations via template table 5.1
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an overview list of all participating organisations (beneficiary and associated partners) using template table 5.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include inter‑relationships (family ties, shared premises, joint ownership, financial interest, overlapping staff/directors) and declare them in the proposal to ensure transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed capacity descriptions for each participating organisation (template 5.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete a separate table for each participating organisation describing capacity; beneficiary table max 1 page, associated partner ½ page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose appropriate role category (Beneficiary; Associated partner linked to beneficiary; Associated partner for outgoing phase (GF only); Associated partner for secondment; Associated partner for non‑academic placement). Include general description, facilities and infrastructure, and highlights of relevant participation in EU projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare PIC and register participants
rubrics_metrics.description: If known, provide the nine‑digit Participant Identification Code (PIC) for beneficiary and associated partners; note that shortlisted proposals require participant registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisations will have to be registered with the EC Participant Register Services if shortlisted; include draft or validated PICs where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tips for describing host institution and research group fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state your faculty/department/research group and outline strengths of host supervisor and wider department and any other parts of the university you will interact with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convey the message that the host is a fantastic match for your project. Provide specific examples of department strengths and expected interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and profile of supervisor (table guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the organisational capacity tables, include supervisor name, title, qualifications, research profile and main highlights, and evidence of experience supervising early career researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include main highlights specific to supervisor/research group (e.g. number of Master/PhD/Postdocs supervised), and emphasize experience in supporting early career researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key research facilities, infrastructure and equipment (table guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate beneficiary has sufficient facilities/infrastructure to offer suitable training environment and knowledge transfer to the researcher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State specifics of facilities and equipment available, emphasize state‑of‑the‑art nature and fully trained staff, mention software licences, and provide concrete examples (desk, computer, library subscriptions). If associated partners are involved, describe nature of the link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous/current involvement in EU and funded programmes
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate up to 5 relevant EU, national or international research and training actions/projects the institution/department has participated in, with main highlights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to demonstrate host experience with EU projects and supporting early career researchers; include numbers supervised and other relevant achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional ethics information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide any extra ethics information not included in Part A of the proposal, if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this section only for supplementary ethics material that could not fit in Part A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional security screening information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide any extra security screening information not included in Part A, if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this section only for supplementary security screening material that could not fit in Part A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental considerations (MSCA Green Charter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the project will strive to adhere to the MSCA Green Charter and reduce environmental impact during implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe concrete measures (e.g. combine online conference attendance with in‑person workshops, coordinate conference attendance with fieldwork) and/or reference institutional measures (NTNU Miljøutviklingsplan 2020–2030). Note: Green Charter is non‑binding and not evaluated, but funded projects will be asked to report application of its principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of commitment for Global Fellowships — minimum requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For Global Fellowships, include scanned letter(s) of commitment from associated partners hosting the outgoing phase meeting minimum requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters must have heading/stamp from institution, be dated not earlier than call publication, demonstrate willingness to participate, and explain precise role. Experts will disregard contributions of associated partners lacking such evidence; absence of letter makes GF proposal inadmissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Template content and signatory authority for letters of commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters should state the organisation's commitment to participate and describe roles/contributions; signatory must be entitled to commit the entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non‑binding exemplar language given: confirm participation and contribution, describe involvement, and include name, date, signature. If the letter lacks sufficient information (no signature, wrong references, outdated), experts may penalise under Implementation criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence — quality and pertinence of R&I objectives (1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe quality and pertinence of research & innovation objectives, ensuring objectives are measurable, verifiable and realistically achievable and that the work goes beyond the state of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address ambition and the extent to which objectives go beyond state of the art; explicitly state measurability and verifiability and justify realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness of the proposed methodology (1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe overall methodology (concepts, models, assumptions), integration of disciplines/methods, consideration of gender/diversity where relevant, and quality of open science practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how methodology enables delivery of project objectives, identify challenges and how to overcome them. If interdisciplinarity is unnecessary, justify. For gender/diversity, state how sex/gender and other diversity aspects are accounted for in research content or justify irrelevance. Describe open science practices implementation and research data management (FAIR principles).

rubrics_metrics.name: AI robustness requirements (when AI is used)
rubrics_metrics.description: If AI systems/techniques are used or developed, demonstrate technical robustness, social robustness, reliability and explainability proportionate to assessed risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI systems should be technically robust, accurate and reproducible; socially robust considering context; reliable and minimize unintended harm; and able to provide suitable explanations of decision‑making where significant impact on people's lives may occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open science practices and research data management
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how appropriate open science practices will be implemented and how research data/outputs will be managed following FAIR principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open science examples: pre‑registration, registered reports, preprints, crowd‑sourcing, reproducibility measures, open access to outputs, open peer‑review, citizen science. Explain chosen practices and adaptations (e.g. up to 1/2 page on RDM). Provide justification if none are appropriate.
